question.problem: A team of $5$ players is to be chosen at random from $7$ boys and $5$ girls.  What is the probability that $2$ boys and $3$ girls will be chosen? Round your answer to the nearest percent.
question.worked_solution:
Let $A$ represent the event described in the question. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A) & =\frac{n}{N},\end{aligned}
$$

where $N$ is the total number of ways to choose $5$ people out of a total of $12,$ and $n$ is the number of picks where $2$ are boys and $3$ are girls.

Since the order in which the players are chosen does not matter, we use combinations.

First, we compute $N.$ The number of ways to pick $5$ people from a total of $12$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}N={}_{12}{C}_{5} & =\frac{12!}{5!\cdot 7!}=792.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $n.$ The computation of $n$ can be divided into two steps: 

- the number of ways to choose $2$ (out of $7$) boys is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{7}{C}_{2}=\frac{7!}{2!\cdot 5!}=21\end{aligned}
$$

- the number of ways to choose $3$ (out of $5$) girls is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{C}_{3} & =\frac{5!}{3!\cdot 2!}=10\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the results from the above steps, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n={}_{7}{C}_{2}\cdot {}_{5}{C}_{3}=21\cdot 10=210.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A) & =\frac{210}{792}≈0.27=27%.\end{aligned}
$$
